cleared.check: Crate pins and op-revm sources of op-reth v2.10.0 (final) and v2.11.0-rc.1 compared with v2.10.0-rc.4, the build in service on Unichain, Ink and Soneium.
cleared.result: v2.10.0 has a Cargo.lock byte equal to rc.4 and identical op-revm sources. v2.11.0-rc.1 pins revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2, revm-bytecode 43.0.0 and ruint 1.20.0 as before; on the interpreter and integer path only reth-evm, reth-revm (2.7.0 to 2.8.1) and revm-inspectors (0.44.0 to 0.44.3) move. Its op-revm differs only in handler.rs, where the deposit mint is added with saturating addition. No release changes an opcode handler, the integer library, jump analysis or the keccak path that src/libraries/FullMath.sol, TickMath.sol, BitMath.sol, SqrtPriceMath.sol or SwapMath.sol reach.

cleared.check: Which instruction set the Lagoon spec id selects in op-revm.
cleared.result: spec.rs maps both KARST and LAGOON to SpecId::OSAKA, so the opcode table, gas schedule and the EIP-7825 transaction gas cap of Karst carry over unchanged. handler.rs has no Lagoon branch. precompiles.rs lagoon() takes karst() and replaces only the BLS12-381 G1 MSM, G2 MSM and pairing entries, which src/ never calls with an input it builds.

cleared.check: Lagoon metering settlement as implemented in alloy-op-evm block/mod.rs at op-reth v2.11.0-rc.1, and the refund policy that ships with it.
cleared.result: post_exec_settlement_deltas computes the refund from the gas the EVM reported after evm.transact returns; apply_post_exec_refund_to_state credits tx.signer() and debits the beneficiary, BASE_FEE_RECIPIENT and OPERATOR_FEE_RECIPIENT, with checked_sub that makes an underflow invalidate the block. Nothing runs EVM code after it, so no PoolManager frame can see the new balances inside the refunded transaction, and src/PoolManager.sol:349-364 credits native only from msg.value. The only policy exported by post_exec/mod.rs is NullRefundPolicy, whose inspect_step is empty and whose finish_tx returns a zero refund.

cleared.check: Whether any path in src/ branches on remaining gas, which a metering refund or a Lagoon gas rule could change.
cleared.result: Outside src/test the only uses of gas() forward all remaining gas to a call: the native transfer and ERC-20 transfer in src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73 and the hook call in src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134. No branch reads gasleft. The metering refund is applied after execution and cannot change what any of these calls returns.

cleared.check: A deposit with value addressed to the PoolManager itself.
cleared.result: The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function and its only payable functions are settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300, 305), both behind onlyWhenUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99). A deposit with value that calls it directly reverts and its mint stays at the deposit's from address. A deposit that calls an attacker's contract can only do what an ordinary transaction does. The saturating mint of v2.11.0-rc.1 changes nothing below a balance of 2^256 minus the mint.

leads.question: On 11 January 2027 after 16:00:01 UTC (or on the Sepolia chains after 10 December 2026), do battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py give the same results at a block past lagoon_time on OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink and Soneium?
leads.why: eth_call with a block time override keeps Karst rules on every endpoint (out/lagoonprobe.json), so no run before activation exercises the Lagoon spec. The source shows the same instruction set; the live run is the only direct check.

leads.question: When an op-reth release ships a refund policy other than NullRefundPolicy (block level warming refunds are described in alloy-op-evm block/mod.rs comments), does its inspect_step only read the interpreter it is given as a mutable reference?
leads.why: A sequencer runs the policy on every transaction it produces. A policy that wrote to the interpreter would make produced blocks differ from verifier execution; that is a liveness risk under operator control, and a write that verifiers also accepted would change PoolManager results.

leadResults.answer: Read op-reth v2.10.0 and v2.11.0-rc.1 (the registry already carries lagoon_time 1799683201; the release source that embeds it could not be fetched, the superchain config archive returned 404). Lagoon in op-revm maps to SpecId::OSAKA, the Karst instruction set, with no new opcode, no handler branch and no change to the EIP-7825 per transaction gas cap. precompiles.rs changes only the three BLS12-381 input limits. Deposit handling changes only in that the mint saturates at the largest balance. The execution side otherwise adds the 0x7D post-execution transaction and the metering settlement after each transaction, whose only shipped policy refunds nothing. The interpreter and integer crates are the same versions as the rc.4 build that every vector and script already ran on. Nothing changes what pool math or a long swap returns on 11 January 2027.

No such block was found. On Zora all 406 blocks with a PoolManager log between 51,570,810 and 54,570,810 hold only the L1 attributes deposit, none failed. The OP Mainnet scan could not finish. mainnet.optimism.io answers eth_getBlockReceipts with 'rpc method is not whitelisted' (queried 2026-11-28), optimism-rpc.publicnode.com found 4,056 blocks with a PoolManager log in the last 60,000 blocks but refused 26 log windows and then the receipt queries with HTTP 403 before the sample of 800 finished (console output of that run; its log was overwritten by the next run), and optimism.drpc.org refused 2,000 block log windows with HTTP 400 (out/l1341-op-sample.log, out/l1341-op-sample-drpc-empty.json). The source settles the question for the PoolManager anyway: native credit comes only from msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354) and each deposit is its own transaction, so a failed deposit's mint cannot reach another transaction's deltas.

No endpoint simulates the mint. OP Mainnet and Zora reject eth_call and eth_estimateGas from an empty account with OutOfFunds and refuse debug_traceCall (not whitelisted, or an API key is needed). optimism.drpc.org and rpc-qnd.inkonchain.com accept debug_traceCall with type 0x7e, mint and sourceHash fields, but the prestate diff shows only the sender's nonce change and no mint or value movement, so the fields are ignored and the call runs as an ordinary call. The row therefore still rests on the specification and on op-revm handler.rs, which credits the mint to the caller before execution and keeps it on failure.
